darkflobi · ledger

darkflobi is the lab's agent (fathom-lab/styxx). since 2026-10-24 a gate at its telegram exits writes one hash-chained line per outbound attempt: hashes, verdicts and counts, never message text or chat ids. every night at 00:00 new york time the day's head is posted in public at t.me/DFledger. this page carries the ledger's bytes and re-derives the chain in your browser: every chain number below is computed here, from the embedded bytes, when you open it; the witness states (the ots column, the witness tile and section) are the tail's store as copied at build: this page parses no proof and asks no explorer.

re-deriving the chain in this browser…

the anchors

each row is the line the gate wrote when it posted a head; the text column is the exact form of the post at t.me/DFledger, to compare by eye or by paste. "in chain" means the entry at that seq carries that digest, no line of that day sits after it, and the ledger's own anchor line agrees. "bitcoin" is the post's OpenTimestamps proof: the bytes' sha256, committed into a bitcoin block by the public calendars — a thing the lab does not control. pending means the calendars hold it and the block has not been mined yet.

paste an anchor post from t.me/DFledger to check it against this chain:

prove a message

paste the text of a message darkflobi sent in public, as copied from telegram, trailer included. the page hashes it the way the gate did (utf-8, lf) and looks for the send line that carries that digest; then it names the day's posted head and the bitcoin proof that fix it. a match says these exact bytes left his gate at that second under that verdict. no match says the text differs from the bytes the gate saw (telegram may drop markdown or change whitespace), or the line is one of the withheld ones, or the message never passed the gate.

the days

public sends by the gate's decision in shadow: clean (every numeral bound, or none present), marked (a numeral with no receipt), would refuse (a lint hit, or what the frozen rule refuses). operator dm lines are counted apart: they are hashes like the rest and outside the measured population.

break it

change one line in a copy and re-derive the copy. a flipped field breaks the next line's link. a forger who then rewrites every later digest gets a copy that re-derives, with a different head, and the heads posted in public no longer match it: that is what the nightly post is for.

the lines

seq · day (new york) · utc · kind · exit · class · payload · decision · reasons · numerals bound of total · entry_id (first 16). "would refuse" is a shadow verdict: the message went out. a started line is a gateway start; a delivered line answers a send line; an anchor line records the posted head; a withheld line shows its digest only.

the raw lines



what this is not


    

  • not a transcript: no message text, no chat id, no session key is in these lines; destinations are salted hashes.
    • 

  • not a truth check: the gate counts numerals and binds the ones that have a committed receipt, and it reads a word list; it does not read whether a sentence is true.
    • 

  • not a proof of completeness: the chain shows that no line was changed, dropped or reordered without the digests disagreeing; it cannot show that every send got a line. the census at the window's close reads the chats for that.
    • 

  • not whole where a line is withheld: a withheld line's digest is published and its fields are not, so you bridge it on the lab's word; the lines between the previous posted head and that line are then not pinned for you. the status line above counts them.
    • 

  • not enforcement yet: the gate runs in shadow (required_present: false on every line). "would refuse" is what it would have blocked; it blocked nothing.
    • 

  • not signed: anyone holding the file can recompute the chain. what fixes the bytes and their order is the daily post at t.me/DFledger, outside the box, and the bitcoin proof of each post's bytes; the clock in the lines is the gate's own statement.
    • 

  • not older than its stamp: a bitcoin proof says the post's bytes existed before a block. a proof made on a later day for an earlier post shows only that the post existed by the stamping day; from the day a post is stamped on, its past is fixed.
    • 

  • not every exit: the gate sits on the telegram exits; what leaves by another route is not on it.
    •
